candidate.blueprint_locator: Physiological Integrity → Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p. 12 (PDF pageno 15): educate clients about medications, administer medications safely, review pertinent medication data and evaluate client response to medication.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Antithrombotic medication teaching within postoperative VTE prevention
candidate.educational_objective: Explain that prescribed anticoagulant prophylaxis after total joint arthroplasty is used to reduce postoperative VTE risk as one component of an individualized prevention plan that also includes appropriate mobility, mechanical measures, and ongoing assessment.

options.A: Hip and knee arthroplasty carry important postoperative DVT and pulmonary-embolism risk, so the prescribed anticoagulant is one part of an individualized prevention plan that may also include early movement and mechanical measures.
options.B: Lower-extremity joint replacement carries little VTE risk, so the anticoagulant is being used mainly to improve surgical-wound healing.
options.C: Once an anticoagulant is prescribed, ankle movement, mobilization, compression measures, and assessment for clot symptoms are unnecessary.
options.D: The same anticoagulant regimen is required for every joint-replacement client regardless of bleeding risk, clotting history, or other clinical factors.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. AAOS identifies blood clots in the leg veins as an important complication after total knee replacement and notes that pulmonary embolism can be life-threatening. AAOS prevention programs may include blood-thinning medication, early foot and ankle movement, compression devices or stockings, and clinical assessment. Current AAOS discussion also emphasizes risk stratification because the choice of chemoprophylaxis is not one-size-fits-all and must balance VTE risk against bleeding and wound risks. B incorrectly minimizes postoperative VTE risk and assigns an unsupported wound-healing purpose to anticoagulation. C is incorrect because pharmacologic prophylaxis does not replace mobility, mechanical prevention, or surveillance. D is incorrect because the prophylactic agent and strategy are individualized. The final item therefore supports the prescribed anticoagulant's role without claiming that one drug or regimen is universally required for every arthroplasty patient.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Current AAOS sources directly support clinically important postoperative VTE risk after total knee arthroplasty, use of blood-thinning medication as one prevention measure, complementary mobility/mechanical measures, and individualized risk-stratified prophylaxis rather than a universal anticoagulant regimen.
